source_title: Endometriosis and chronic pelvic pain have similar impact on women, but time to diagnosis is decreasing: an Australian survey (Armour M et al.)
caveat: Online survey shared by endometriosis organisations on social media (non-representative). Surgical diagnosis was self-reported and could not be checked. Total = 2.9 years symptoms to first doctor + 4.9 years first doctor to diagnosis; the paper reports the total as eight years. No SD given for the total. Cited by AIHW.

caveat: SD 7.7. Online survey recruited through social media and endometriosis organisations (non-representative). Self-reported diagnosis. The abstract doesn't say where the delay is counted from. Full text not checked (site blocked).

source_title: Endometriosis-associated symptoms and diagnostic delay: an online survey (Moradi M et al.)
caveat: Preprint; peer-reviewed version not confirmed. SD 6.2. Online survey (non-representative); 86.5% reported surgical confirmation. More than 10 years old. Start point not stated in the abstract. Not used on the site.

source_title: Patient perspectives of healthcare for premenstrual dysphoric disorder in Australia: a mixed-methods study (Border G, Miller YD)
caveat: Recruited through online PMDD support groups and social media (non-representative). Most respondents already diagnosed, so people still undiagnosed are missing. Average of 5 providers seen before diagnosis. Read from the Life in Mind research summary, not the paper. A QUT data record lists 296 participants and fieldwork Nov 2023–Jan 2024; the gap isn't explained. Not used on the site yet.

source_title: Delayed diagnosis and a lack of information associated with dissatisfaction in women with polycystic ovary syndrome (Gibson-Helm M et al.)
source_publisher: Journal of Clinical Endocrinology and Metabolism 102(2):604–612
caveat: No years figure: 33.6% reported more than 2 years before diagnosis; 47.1% saw 3 or more health professionals. Recruited through support-group websites; 53% North America, 42% Europe. Start point not confirmed (full text blocked).

source_title: Pathways to the diagnosis of epithelial ovarian cancer in Australia (Jordan SJ et al.)
caveat: No years figure: 66% diagnosed within 1 month of first presentation, 80% within 3 months, 12% after more than 6 months. Population-based telephone interviews (representative). More than 10 years old.

source_title: Reducing time to diagnosis does not improve outcomes for women with symptomatic ovarian cancer (Nagle CM et al.)
caveat: No years figure: 55% saw a doctor within 1 month of symptoms, 70% within 2 months, 92% within 6 months (time to first doctor, not to diagnosis). Same cohort as Jordan 2010. More than 10 years old. Longer delay was not linked to worse survival. DOI not confirmed; abstract only.
